note.headline: SPY and QQQ fall to new 1-month lows as breadth drops to 12%

summary.thesis: Both indices are in downtrends. Each closed below its 50-day and 200-day averages and below the 1-month low set on Nov 19. Only 12% of stocks are above their 50-day averages. The fear gauge was 'elevated' as of Nov 19. The trend, fear and breadth readings all point the same way: down.
summary.decision: Stand aside, for both long-term buying and swing trades.

note.happening: On Nov 20, SPY closed at 689.81, down 3.64% from 715.87. QQQ closed at 608.45, down 5.67% from 645.04. Both previous closes were the 1-month lows set on Nov 19, so both indices set new 1-month lows today. Over five days SPY is down 8.56% and QQQ is down 10.51%. Over 20 days SPY is down 9.23% and QQQ is down 13.62%. Both 1-month highs came on Oct 28: 772.31 for SPY and 725.61 for QQQ. Both indices had their highest close of the past year on Oct 6: 779.09 for SPY and 759.66 for QQQ. No news has been reported since the last note. Tech (QQQ) is falling faster than the broad market (SPY).
note.business: Trend: both indices are below their 50-day and 200-day averages, so the trend is down for both. QQQ is 12.1% below its 200-day average and SPY is 5.9% below its own. Fear: the VIX closed in the 20–30 'elevated' band on Nov 19 and was at the 99th percentile of its last 252 daily readings. The Nov 20 VIX reading isn't stored yet. Breadth: only 12% of stocks are above their 50-day average, so the selling is broad and not limited to a few large names. Together: prices are falling, fear is high and few stocks are holding up. All three readings say the same thing, and none of them signals a recovery yet.

worth.text: DATA contains no valuation for the market. The levels in this note mark price trends only. They are not estimates of fair value.
worth.key_assumption: No valuation is implied. The levels are price-trend markers only.

bull: SPY's declines are smaller than QQQ's: 9.23% versus 13.62% over 20 days, and 3.64% versus 5.67% today. The broad market is less damaged than tech.

General knowledge, not from DATA: very high fear readings and very low breadth have sometimes appeared near short-term selling washouts. The VIX at the 99th percentile of its past year and breadth at 12% are both extreme readings.

The levels that would show repair are clear. A QQQ close above 645.04 would mean its recent low is holding. A QQQ close above 682.07 would end the tech downtrend. The Nov 25 releases on GDP and PCE inflation could shift sentiment either way.
bear: Both indices closed below their 1-month lows. By the pipeline's definition, that means the decline is continuing.
Only 12% of stocks are above their 50-day average, down from 17% in the previous note. Weakness is spreading.
QQQ is 12.1% below its 200-day gate at 682.07 and 16.8% below its 50-day average at 710.88. The gate is far from the current price.

levels.what: QQQ 200-day average and the market gate. A close above it ends the tech downtrend, which would support a selective stance.
QQQ 1-month low (Nov 19). QQQ closed 6.0% below it. A close back above it would mean the recent low is holding.
QQQ 50-day average. A close above it would put tech's short-term trend back up and pass the pipeline's market check. That would be the cue to lean in more.
QQQ 1-month high (Oct 28). A close above it would mean the tech pullback is fully recovered.
SPY 1-month low (Nov 19). SPY closed 3.8% below it. A close back above it would mean the recent low is holding.
SPY 200-day average. A close above it would put the broad market's long-term trend back up.
SPY 50-day average. A close above it would put SPY's short-term trend back up.
SPY 1-month high (Oct 28). A close above it would mean SPY's pullback is fully recovered.

longterm.why: QQQ remains below its 200-day gate of 682.07. Both indices set new 1-month lows. Breadth is 12% and fear is elevated. All three readings argue against new buying until QQQ closes above 682.07.

swing.why: QQQ closed at 608.45, 16.8% below its 50-day average of 710.88. Below that level, setups keep failing the pipeline's market check.

decision.timing: Two releases are due Nov 25 at 08:30. One is the second estimate of Q3 GDP and corporate profits. The other is October Personal Income and Outlays, which includes PCE, the Fed's preferred inflation measure. The fear reading here is from Nov 19 because the Nov 20 VIX isn't stored yet. The nearest levels to watch are QQQ 645.04 and SPY 715.87.

change_mind: Toward selective: a QQQ close above 682.07, its 200-day average and the market gate. That would end the tech downtrend. Before that, a QQQ close back above 645.04 and an SPY close back above 715.87 would show the recent lows holding.

Toward lean in: a QQQ close above 710.88, its 50-day average, which would pass the pipeline's market check. An SPY close above 760.03 would mean the same for the broad market, together with breadth recovering from 12% and the VIX leaving the 'elevated' band.
note.what_changed: The decision is unchanged from the Nov 19 note: stand aside. Since then, SPY fell 3.64% and QQQ fell 5.67%, and both closed below the Nov 19 closes that now mark their 1-month lows. Breadth fell from 17% to 12%. The moving averages shifted. QQQ's 200-day gate went from 682.01 to 682.07 and its 50-day average from 713.0 to 710.88. SPY's 200-day average went from 730.2 to 730.29 and its 50-day average from 761.48 to 760.03. The VIX reading has moved forward from Nov 18 to Nov 19 and is still 'elevated'. No new news has been reported.
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: Tesla drops 7.64% to 345.82, breaks support; margins and cash still shrinking, avoid

summary.thesis: Tesla is a grade D business whose sales growth has stalled while margins and free cash flow are shrinking, yet the stock is still priced at 380.5 times earnings.
summary.decision: Long-term: avoid; swing: no trade, because today's break below 364.02 confirmed the downtrend.
summary.act_at: No position above 293.94; re-examine at 293.94–299.52 only after the 2027-01-27 report

note.happening: Tesla fell 7.64% to 345.82, down from 374.41. It closed below the 364.02–368.6 zone, which has held 4 times, and now sits in a 337.24–345.88 zone, below its 20-, 50- and 200-day averages (384.8, 375.64, 381.66). Our data shows no news since the last note, so nothing reported explains the drop. The next earnings report is due 2027-01-27.
note.business: Today's drop is a price move, not a business event. No filing or news in our data changed the business today. The business trend is still weak. Sales in the latest quarter grew -0.17% from a year earlier, down from 15.78% two quarters ago. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, fell to 3.35% from 4.74%. Trailing free cash flow, the cash left after investment, fell to 3.3B from 6.8B. Filings show inventory up 15% while latest-quarter sales were up 0%. Unsold cars can force price cuts, which would squeeze margins further. Each dollar invested now earns 5¢ a year, down from 33¢ three years ago. What is not at risk is survival: Tesla has 37.5B of net cash (cash minus debt) and 45.4B of total liquidity. Demand, margins and cash conversion are at risk. The balance sheet is not.

worth.text: At 345.82, Tesla's market value is 1367.0B. That is 13.2 times sales and 380.5 times trailing earnings of 0.91 per share. Our data says the price needs about 51% a year growth, while the company delivered 3% a year over 3 years. A discounted-cash-flow model values a business by the cash it will produce. Starting from 3.3B of free cash flow, it gives 19.98 to 44.11 per share, with a base of 24.59. Even 30% starting growth only reaches 44.46. The other method asks what the stock would be worth at its own past price-to-sales levels. It gives 203.8 to 399.81, with a middle of 293.94. Today's price-to-sales sits at the 72nd percentile of its own 5 years. The whole gap between the methods comes from one choice: value Tesla on the cash it makes, or on the sales multiple the market has historically granted. With quarterly growth at -0.17% and margins falling, the upper part of that historical range is hard to justify. I place fair value between the low and middle of the own-history range.
worth.key_assumption: The market keeps valuing Tesla on its own 5-year price-to-sales history, but at the low-to-middle level that stalled growth justifies, not on its 3.3B of free cash flow.

bull: The balance sheet is strong: 37.5B of net cash and 45.4B of liquidity fund heavy spending without stress.
Trailing revenue still grew to 103.6B from 95.6B, an 8.3% gain over twelve months.
Analysts' next-year EPS growth of 25% (from the valuation assumptions) would point to a recovery in earnings if delivered.
bear: Operating margin fell to 3.35% from 4.74%, and trailing free cash flow halved to 3.3B from 6.8B.
Inventory rose 15% while latest-quarter sales rose 0%, a setup that can force price cuts.
At 380.5 times earnings the price needs about 51% a year growth, against 3% a year delivered over 3 years.

levels.what: Today's close. It is still above the own-history middle of 293.94 and far above the DCF base of 24.59.
Top of the only support zone (295.24–299.52), the first place where buyers have stepped in before.
Middle of the own-history price-to-sales range. Re-examine here only if the 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 3.35%.

longterm.why: Growth has stalled, and margins and cash flow are shrinking, yet the price still assumes a high multiple. The business is graded D, and the committee call is Reduce.

swing.why: Yesterday's trigger, a close below 364.02, fired today, and the direction it showed is down. Price is below every average, with resistance just above at 349.33–354.05 and the next support far below at 295.24–299.52. No trade until a close above 354.05 or a hold at 295.24–299.52.

decision.timing: No new long-term position before the 2027-01-27 report, the next test of margins, inventory and cash. Options priced a 11.6% move by 2026-12-18 and 19.5% by 2027-02-19, but they were set before today's drop, on a 374.41 price.

change_mind: The 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 4.74% and quarterly sales growth back above -0.17%.
Trailing free cash flow climbs back toward 6.8B from 3.3B, with inventory growth no longer outpacing sales.
For a swing, a close above 354.05 that then clears 368.6; for the long term, a price at or below 293.94 with margins holding at 3.35% or better.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still avoid and no trade; today's 7.64% drop to 345.82, a close below 364.02, confirmed the downtrend that yesterday's note expected.
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: NVIDIA plunges 14% to 125.53 on governance fears; still wait, buy at 114.29

summary.thesis: The business is still growing fast and earning more cash than a year ago, but legal and leadership news, plus a margin at a 5-year peak, leave the stock with no floor in the chart yet.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait, and buy at 114.29, the price that already allows for operating margin falling to 48%. Swing: no trade, because there is no support level to set a stop under.
summary.act_at: buy at 114.29; back to hold on a close above 150.14

note.happening: NVIDIA fell 14.01% to 125.53. CNBC reported this ended its longest weekly losing streak since 2008. On 2026-11-19, CNBC reported that California's attorney general sent NVIDIA a subpoena (a legal demand for documents) in a probe of chips reportedly diverted to China. CNBC also reported that Jensen Huang will testify publicly before a Senate banking panel. TechCrunch's reports of a CEO exit are marked speculative and are not confirmed by any filing.
note.business: Nothing in today's news is a reported change in demand, margins or cash. The last filed quarter (ended 2026-07-26) showed sales up 105.85% from a year earlier, gross margin at 74.67%, and operating margin up to 65.21% from 58.09%. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) was 127.0B over the trailing year, up from 72.0B. Net cash is 23.2B. Analysts have kept raising estimates: next-year EPS of 16.61 is up 4.3% in 30 days. What changed is governance and legal risk: a state subpoena, a Senate hearing and an unconfirmed leadership change. The FT reported that the US approved some chip sales to Chinese companies, which may help demand, but it is not in any filing. Three risks already sat in the filings before today. First, the 65% operating margin is at the top of its 5-year range (16–65%). Second, unpaid customer bills grew 127% while sales grew 106%, which can mean sales were pulled forward or customers are stretched. Third, insiders sold $946.6M outside pre-set plans. The cash and current growth are not at risk today. The peak margin and the quality of receivables are.

worth.text: At 125.53, the stock trades at 15.8 times trailing earnings and 7.6 times next year's estimated earnings. Its price-to-sales ratio is 10.0, against a peer median of 15.3, and sits at the 4.0 percentile of its own 5-year range, which is cheap compared with almost all of its recent past. The cash-flow model (DCF, which values future free cash flow in today's money) gives 190.68 / 221.52 / 262.77 for its bear, base and bull cases. Its own-history sales multiples give 217.35–411.04. The data's summary line still quotes the prior close of 145.98, not today's price. The assumption that drives the gap is how fast free cash flow grows from 127.0B. The model caps starting growth at 30%, which gives 221.52. At 20% growth the value is 152.07, and at 10% it is 102.96. Today's price implies about 15.0% starting growth. The second driver is margin: at 20% growth, value falls to 114.29 if operating margin drops to 48%, and to 76.52 if it drops to 32%. So the price assumes either slower growth or some margin fade, but not both together.
worth.key_assumption: Operating margin stays near 65.21% instead of fading toward 48%, while free cash flow grows from 127.0B at a starting rate of 20% or more.

bull: The stock trades at 7.6 times next year's estimated EPS of 16.61, and that estimate is up 27.7% in 90 days.
Free cash flow rose to 127.0B from 72.0B, with 23.2B of net cash, so the company does not need outside money.
Price-to-sales of 10.0 is below the peer median of 15.3 and at the 4.0 percentile of its own 5-year history.
bear: Operating margin of 65.21% is at the top of its 5-year range of 16–65%. If it falls to 48%, the model value drops to 114.29, and at 32% it drops to 76.52.
Unpaid customer bills grew 127% while sales grew 106%, a sign that sales may have been pulled forward.
The trend is down, with price far below the 20-day average of 181.46 and the 50-day average of 207.0. No support level appears below 125.53.

levels.what: The value if operating margin falls to 48%. Buy at 114.29 if next-year EPS estimates hold near 16.61, because that price already allows for a large margin fade.
The top of the nearest resistance zone (147.46–150.14). A close above it would end the breakdown and return the call to hold.
The model value at 20% starting growth. Holding above it would mean the market again prices the margin as durable.

longterm.why: The automated rule says 'Buy now', but the committee says 'Hold' and the macro and technical views are negative. Most of the gap to fair value depends on a peak margin, and the governance news is unresolved, so the entry is at the level that assumes margin fade.

swing.why: There is no support level below 125.53 to set a stop under. The nearest resistance at 147.46 is about two ATRs (average daily range, 10.71) away, which is too wide for a defined-risk trade. No trade until a close above 150.14.

decision.timing: There is no earnings date in our data. Huang's Senate testimony (no date in our data), the California subpoena, and the next quarterly filing, which will show whether margin and receivables hold, are the events that could move the price. As of 2026-11-19, options priced a 12.1% move by the 2026-12-18 expiry.

change_mind: A close above 150.14 would move the long-term call back to hold and open a swing entry.
If the next filing shows operating margin below the prior 58.09%, or receivables still growing faster than sales, the buy level would shift down toward 76.52.
If next-year EPS estimates fall back below the 30-day-ago level of 15.91, the buy at 114.29 would be cancelled.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait with a buy at the 48%-margin value, now 114.29, because the 14.01% drop to 125.53 left no support below the price and added legal and leadership risk without changing the business numbers.
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: AMD falls 13.25% to 424.39 in AI selloff; still above fair value

summary.thesis: AMD's business is getting stronger, with faster sales growth, higher margins and more cash, but even after two days of steep falls the price is still well above every estimate of fair value in our data.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait, because the stock only becomes a value buy at or below 333.38; swing: wait, because the price has no clear direction and sits between support and resistance.
summary.act_at: Long-term buy at or below 333.38; swing only after a hold of 392.05–403.41 or a close above 460.21

note.happening: AMD fell 13.25% to 424.39. CNBC reported a broad AI selloff that pulled Nvidia and AMD shares down. The Financial Times reported that the US approved sales of Nvidia and AMD chips to Chinese companies. The next earnings report is on 2027-02-02.
note.business: Today's fall changes sentiment, not the business. The latest filed quarter (filed 2026-11-04) was strong. Sales grew 44.68% from a year earlier, up from 37.85% two quarters ago. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, rose to 17.72% from 8.78%. Free cash flow, the cash left after investment, reached 7.1B over the last 12 months, up from 5.4B. The company holds 8.7B more cash than debt, so its balance sheet is not at risk. Analysts raised their earnings estimates by 11.29% over the last 30 days. The reported China approval could add demand if it holds, but no filing confirms it yet. Two real risks to the business come from the filings. Inventory rose 57% while sales rose 45%, and unsold chips can force price cuts. The 18% operating margin is also near the top of its 5-year range of -2% to 22%. Margins that high often fall back. What the selloff threatens is the price, which still assumes years of very fast growth.

worth.text: At 424.39, AMD trades at 92.5 times its past 12 months of earnings and 24.1 times what analysts expect next year. The low next-year figure only works if earnings per share reach 17.64, up from 4.59 over the last 12 months. That is the 118% growth the model notes. The price is 15.3 times sales, against a peer median of 12.2, and sits at the 90th percentile of AMD's own 5-year range. The cash-flow model (DCF) values the shares at 144.7 to 219.03, with 185.36 in the middle case. Based on its own past price-to-sales ratios, AMD would be worth 179.24 to 333.38. The gap between these numbers and the price comes down to one input: how fast cash flow grows at the start. The model caps that at 30%, which gives 185.36. The current price implies 53.9% growth. If the operating margin fell to 13%, the value would drop to 97.82.
worth.key_assumption: Starting cash-flow growth: the price implies 53.9%, while the model caps it at 30% (185.36 a share), so the price depends on analysts' 118% next-year earnings growth coming true.

bull: Analysts raised next-year EPS to 17.64 from 15.85 a month ago, an 11.3% upgrade.
Operating margin roughly doubled to 17.72% from 8.78%, and sales growth sped up to 44.68%.
Free cash flow rose to 7.1B from 5.4B, and the company holds 8.7B in net cash.
bear: The price of 424.39 is above the highest fair value of 333.38 and implies 53.9% starting cash-flow growth.
Inventory rose 57% while sales rose 45%, which could force price cuts on unsold chips.
If the operating margin falls to 13%, value drops to 97.82; the stock trades at 15.3 times sales against a peer median of 12.2.

levels.what: Today's close. It is above every valuation method, so it is not a buy price.
Bottom of the 392.05–403.41 support zone. A close below it would mean the selloff is deepening, though the price would still be above fair value.
Top of the fair-value range. The case for buying on value starts here.

longterm.why: The business keeps improving, but even after two big down days the price is far above the highest fair value of 333.38. The price only makes sense if growth runs well above the model's 30% cap.

swing.why: The price sits just below its 200-day average of 429.79 and far below its 20-day (509.08) and 50-day (553.1) averages, with no clear trend. The average daily range (ATR) is 45.41, so one normal day could reach the 392.05–403.41 support or the 460.21 resistance. A trade needs either a hold above 392.05 or a close above 460.21.

decision.timing: Earnings on 2027-02-02 are more than two months away, but options price a 17.5% move by 2026-12-18. More AI-selloff or China headlines could reach the support or resistance zones before then.

change_mind: Buy on value if the price closes at or below 333.38 while analysts' next-year EPS estimate stays near 17.64.
Change to avoid if the 2027-02-02 report shows the operating margin falling from 17.72% toward 13%, where value drops to 97.82, or if inventory keeps growing faster than sales.
A swing entry becomes possible on a close above 460.21, or if the price holds the 392.05–403.41 support after a test.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: wait on both horizons; today's 13.25% drop to 424.39 still leaves the price above the 333.38 top of fair value.
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: Amazon drops 4.1% to 246.82, nears value; still waiting for 238.65

summary.thesis: Amazon is growing and its margins are improving, but it is burning cash and its growth has slowed, so the price is only fair at about 238.65, not at 246.82.
summary.decision: Long term: wait for 238.65. Swing: no new trade unless the price holds the 232.99–238.97 support zone.

note.happening: Amazon fell 4.1% to 246.82. That puts it right at its 200-day average of 245.15 and below its 20-day (257.42) and 50-day (255.03) averages, all of which are flat. The only news since the last note is two reported Black Friday deal headlines from The Verge, and neither one matters to the business. The data has no earnings date, and the latest filing was on 2026-10-30.
note.business: Nothing in today's news changes the business. The drop is about sentiment: the macro agent describes a tech market in a downtrend with elevated fear. The business facts come from the last filing. Sales are still growing: trailing revenue is 797.5B, up from 691.3B. But quarterly growth slowed to 12.09% from 16.61% two quarters ago, and it rose only 0.67% from the prior quarter. Margins improved, with operating margin at 13.09% vs 11.02%, though the filings flag that 13% is the top of its 5-year range of 2–13%. Cash is the weak spot. Free cash flow (cash left after paying for the business and its investments) swung to -46.9B from 10.6B. Net debt is 66.7B (cash 55.8B vs debt 180.9B). Unpaid customer bills rose 61% while sales rose 12%, which may mean sales are being pulled forward or customers are stretched. Short-term funding is not at risk, with 114.2B of liquidity. What is at risk is the claim that heavy spending will turn into cash, and margins holding near their peak.

worth.text: There is no DCF (a value based on future cash) because free cash flow is negative, so the only method is Amazon's own price-to-sales history. That method puts fair value at 187.93 (20th percentile), 238.65 (50th) and 265.96 (80th). At 246.82 the price sits between the middle and the top. It trades at 3.3 times sales, the 68th percentile of its own 5 years, and at 20.0 times trailing earnings and 19.3 times this year's. The gap between methods comes from which yardstick you use. Against peers, 3.3 times sales looks cheap next to their median of 6.3, and growth-adjusted it is 0.62 of peers. But the filings note that the price implies about 34% a year growth, against 13% a year delivered over 3 years. Next year's estimated earnings per share of 10.67 is below this year's 12.8, which lifts the multiple to 23.1. Note that the valuation summary in the data still quotes yesterday's 257.37.
worth.key_assumption: Amazon's price-to-sales stays within its own 5-year range instead of moving toward the peer median of 6.3.

bull: It trades at 3.3 times sales vs a peer median of 6.3, and growth-adjusted it is 0.62 of peers.
Operating margin rose to 13.09% from 11.02% while trailing revenue grew to 797.5B from 691.3B.
Analysts raised next-year earnings estimates 1.4% over 30 days, to 10.67 per share.
bear: Free cash flow fell to -46.9B from 10.6B, leaving net debt of 66.7B.
Quarterly sales growth slowed to 12.09% from 16.61% two quarters ago, while unpaid customer bills rose 61%.
Next-year earnings per share of 10.67 is below this year's 12.8, which pushes the forward P/E to 23.1 from 19.3.

levels.what: Middle of the own-history value range, which is also the top of the 232.99–238.97 support zone (4 touches). This is the main buy level.
The 200-day average, right under today's price. A small first entry here only if the next filing shows free cash flow better than -46.9B.
Top of the own-history value range. No buying above it.

longterm.why: The price fell toward fair value but is still above 238.65, while cash burn and slowing growth are unresolved. The business grade is D and the committee call is 'Reduce'.

swing.why: At 246.82 the price is in the middle of its 244.3–249.71 zone. Resistance at 251.93–257.04 is less than one typical day's move away (the ATR, or average daily range, is 9.97), and the macro view is a tech downtrend. There is no trade unless the price pulls back into 232.99–238.97 and holds, or closes above 257.04.

decision.timing: With no earnings date in the data, price levels set the timing. Options to 2026-12-18 price in a move of about 8.8%, priced off 257.37 before today's drop, and the most open put interest sits at the 240 and 230 strikes.

change_mind: The next filing shows free cash flow better than -46.9B and quarterly growth above 12.09%. In that case, buy at 245.15 instead of waiting for 238.65.
A close below 226.88, the bottom of the lower support zone, would turn the long-term action from wait to avoid until the price is near 187.93.
Next-year earnings estimates fall back below 10.5 (the level 90 days ago). That would remove the one improving estimate, and in that case no buying above 232.99.

note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: Microsoft falls 2.77% to 484.52, breaking support; hold, add nearer 475.73

summary.thesis: The business keeps getting better, but free cash flow fell from 78.0B to 60.0B, so the price only makes sense if heavy spending starts paying back.
summary.decision: Hold. Add only near the low end of the stock's usual valuation range, and leave the swing trade alone until price picks a side.

note.happening: Microsoft fell 2.77% to 484.52. It closed below the 486.0–491.22 zone, which had 8 touches and was yesterday's add level. That zone now sits overhead as resistance, a price area where selling has capped rallies. There is no news since the last note, and the next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
note.business: Today's drop is about price, not the business. There is no news, so nothing about demand, margins or competition changed today. The latest filed quarter is still solid. Sales grew 18.8% from a year earlier, up from 18.3% two quarters ago. The operating margin (the share of sales left after running costs) rose to 47.1% from 46.27%. The balance sheet has 29.0B more cash than debt, and the share count shrank 0.27%. Analysts keep raising their numbers. The next-year earnings-per-share estimate rose to 24.2 from 23.68 thirty days ago. Cash is the weak spot. Free cash flow, the cash left after investment, fell to 60.0B from 78.0B, and only 17.31% of sales turns into free cash. The filings say each dollar invested now earns 30¢ a year, down from 51¢ three years ago. The spending is real, but it is not paying back yet (general knowledge: much of it is reported to be AI data-center build-out). Earnings power is not at risk. The risk is that cash returns on that spending stay low for longer than the price assumes.

worth.text: The price is 25.3 times trailing earnings and 20.0 times next year's estimate. It is also 10.4 times sales, against a peer median of 3.5. A discounted cash flow model values a business on its future cash, discounted back to today. Starting from today's 60.0B of free cash flow, it gives 180.1 to 286.88 per share, with a base of 217.44. To justify the current price, free cash flow would have to start growing at about 39.7% a year. Even 30% starting growth only gets to 341.8. Against its own past, the picture is different. Using its usual 5-year price-to-sales range, the stock is worth 475.73 to 592.92, with a middle of 535.43. Today's price-to-sales sits at the 33rd percentile of its own 5-year history.
